commands.name: 🌀 cURL Cheatsheet
commands.snippet:
# GET request
curl http://target.com

# GET with verbose output
curl -v http://target.com

# GET with silent mode (no progress bar)
curl -s http://target.com

# Follow redirects
curl -L http://target.com

# Save output to file
curl -o output.html http://target.com

# Save with remote filename
curl -O http://target.com/file.zip

# POST with data
curl -X POST -d 'param1=value1&param2=value2' http://target.com/login

# POST with JSON
curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"user":"admin","pass":"password"}' http://target.com/api

# PUT request
curl -X PUT -d 'data=value' http://target.com/resource/1

# DELETE request
curl -X DELETE http://target.com/resource/1

# PATCH request
curl -X PATCH -d '{"key":"value"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' http://target.com/resource/1

# OPTIONS (check allowed methods)
curl -X OPTIONS -v http://target.com

# Add custom header
curl -H 'X-Custom-Header: value' http://target.com

# Set User-Agent
curl -A 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)' http://target.com

# Set Referer
curl -e 'http://google.com' http://target.com

# Set multiple headers
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -H 'Accept: application/json' http://target.com/api

# View response headers only
curl -I http://target.com

# View request + response headers
curl -v -s http://target.com 2>&1 | grep -E '^[<>]'

# Basic auth
curl -u username:password http://target.com

# Basic auth (prompt for password)
curl -u username http://target.com

# Bearer token
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN' http://target.com/api

# Digest auth
curl --digest -u username:password http://target.com

# NTLM auth
curl --ntlm -u username:password http://target.com

# API key in header
curl -H 'X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY' http://target.com/api

# Send a cookie
curl -b 'session=abc123' http://target.com

# Save cookies to file
curl -c cookies.txt http://target.com

# Load and send cookies from file
curl -b cookies.txt http://target.com

# Save and resend cookies (full session)
curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt http://target.com

# Upload a file (multipart form)
curl -F 'file=@/path/to/file.txt' http://target.com/upload

# Upload file with MIME type
curl -F 'file=@shell.php;type=image/jpeg' http://target.com/upload

# Upload via PUT
curl -T /path/to/file.txt http://target.com/upload

# Download file
curl -O http://target.com/file.zip

# Resume interrupted download
curl -C - -O http://target.com/largefile.zip

# Download with speed limit
curl --limit-rate 100K -O http://target.com/file.zip

# Ignore SSL certificate errors
curl -k https://target.com

# Specify CA certificate
curl --cacert /path/to/ca.crt https://target.com

# Use client certificate
curl --cert /path/to/client.crt --key /path/to/client.key https://target.com

# Force TLS version
curl --tlsv1.2 https://target.com
curl --tlsv1.3 https://target.com

# Route through HTTP proxy
curl -x http://127.0.0.1:8080 http://target.com

# Route through SOCKS5 proxy
curl --socks5 127.0.0.1:1080 http://target.com

# Proxy with credentials
curl -x http://user:pass@proxyhost:8080 http://target.com

# Route through Burp Suite
curl -k -x http://127.0.0.1:8080 https://target.com

# Check HTTP methods
curl -X OPTIONS -v http://target.com 2>&1 | grep -i allow

# Grab banner / server info
curl -I http://target.com

# Test for open redirect
curl -v -L 'http://target.com/redirect?url=http://evil.com'

# Directory brute-force (loop)
for dir in admin login dashboard api; do echo "$dir: $(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://target.com/$dir)"; done

# Test SSRF
